dimensions.name: Cyclomatic Complexity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How tangled the control flow is — methods with many branches are hard to test and change.

dimensions.name: Cognitive Complexity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How hard the code is for a person to follow, beyond raw branching.

dimensions.name: God Classes
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Over-large classes that try to do too much ("god classes").

dimensions.name: Code Duplication
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How much of the production code is copy-pasted: the share of production lines inside a reported copy (every copy of a duplicated block or of an edited member, each line once), 10 at none and 0 at a quarter of the lines.

dimensions.name: Coupling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether volatile projects sit underneath others that depend on them (so their churn ripples upward), and whether project dependencies form cycles. A widely-depended-on but stable shared/kernel project is healthy, not penalised.

dimensions.name: Cohesion (LCOM4)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a class's methods are focused on a single responsibility.

dimensions.name: Architectural Integrity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code respects its intended layering / architecture rules.

dimensions.name: Code Coverage
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How much of the code is actually exercised by tests.

dimensions.name: Test Quality
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the tests truly assert behaviour rather than just running the code.

dimensions.name: Test Reliability
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the tests pass reliably, with no flakiness.

dimensions.name: Dependency Hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether dependencies are current, not deprecated, and not bloated. Known vulnerabilities are D30's.

dimensions.name: Secret Scanning
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any secrets (keys, tokens, passwords) have leaked into the code.

dimensions.name: License Compliance
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the licenses of third-party packages are compatible with your policy.

dimensions.name: Churn × Complexity Hotspots
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Files that change often and are also complex — the riskiest hotspots.

dimensions.name: Bus Factor
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether knowledge is concentrated in too few people (the "bus factor").

dimensions.name: Explicit Debt
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Acknowledged debt left in the code — TODOs, dead code, suppressed warnings.

dimensions.name: Solution Shape
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the solution is laid out in a sensible, conventional structure.

dimensions.name: Documentation Quality
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the project's documentation is clear, complete, and useful.

dimensions.name: ADR Quality
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether architecture decisions are recorded well (context, decision, consequences).

dimensions.name: Naming Consistency
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether names — types, methods, variables — are clear and consistent.

dimensions.name: Internal API Consistency
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the internal API surface is consistent and coherent.

dimensions.name: Boundary Type-Coupling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether domain types (IDs, enums, value objects) leak across bounded-context boundaries.

dimensions.name: Comment Value
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether comments are worth it — explaining WHY (valuable) rather than WHAT (redundant).

dimensions.name: ADR Conformance
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code actually follows the decisions recorded in the project's ADRs.

dimensions.name: Project Cohesion
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether each project is a focused, coherent unit rather than an oversized grab-bag.

dimensions.name: Navigability
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How far you must trace to follow a call — low indirection and co-located slices read easier.

dimensions.name: Secrets (history)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any secrets were ever committed — scanned across the full git history, not just now.

dimensions.name: Static Analysis (SAST)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Real static-analysis (SAST) findings — likely security bugs in the code, any language.

dimensions.name: Dependency Vulnerabilities
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any dependency of the repository, direct or transitive, in any package ecosystem the repository declares (for example npm, PyPI, Maven or Cargo), is affected at the version in use by a known published vulnerability, as recorded in a security advisory (for example a CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) entry or a GHSA (GitHub Security Advisory) entry). A match of the version in use against the advisories known at the time of reading: not proof that the vulnerable code is reached or exploitable, and no match does not mean the dependencies are free of vulnerabilities.

dimensions.name: IaC & Container Security
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether Dockerfiles / Terraform / Kubernetes config follow security best practices.

dimensions.name: Data Compliance (PII/GDPR)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Likely personal-data (PII / GDPR) handling concerns — logging or storing data without safeguards.

dimensions.name: Knowledge Freshness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether anyone still has living knowledge of each file, or it has been orphaned — last understood long ago by someone now gone quiet. The sibling of the bus factor: D16 asks who owns it, D34 asks whether anyone still knows it.

dimensions.name: Change Coupling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether files that change together actually belong together: pairs that repeatedly co-change in recent git history despite having no explicit code dependency, surfacing the hidden/logical coupling (and boundaries in the wrong place) a static scan can't see. A pair is read over the last 20 changes of the less often changed of its two files, and only while the two have changed together within the year before the analysed commit, so a coupling that is broken leaves the reading.

dimensions.name: Supply-chain Provenance & Signing
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the build pipeline, including the configuration that publishes its releases, provides supply-chain integrity: generated provenance or attestation (a record, often signed, of how and from what an artifact was built), signed artifacts, an SBOM (software bill of materials, a machine-readable list of the components in an artifact), and build actions the pipeline reuses (for example CI actions or included templates) pinned to an immutable reference, such as a full commit hash or digest, rather than a movable tag or branch. Presence of the configuration, not a runtime guarantee.

dimensions.name: Vulnerability-disclosure Policy
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the repository publishes a coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure policy (SECURITY.md or security.txt) with a reporting contact, so finders know how to report a vulnerability. Presence of a policy file with a contact, not whether the policy is adequate or honoured.

dimensions.name: Network Egress Confinement
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether Kubernetes workloads restrict network EGRESS with a NetworkPolicy (or Cilium policy), limiting where a compromised pod can send data or reach a command-and-control server. Presence of committed egress-restricting policy, not runtime enforcement.

dimensions.name: Kernel & Syscall Confinement
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether Kubernetes workloads confine the kernel boundary — a seccomp profile (RuntimeDefault/Localhost) plus an AppArmor/SELinux mandatory-access-control layer — shrinking the syscall attack surface a container escape would use. Presence of committed confinement config, not runtime enforcement.

dimensions.name: Runtime Threat Enforcement
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the Kubernetes deployment commits runtime threat controls: a threat-detection engine that watches running workloads and alerts on suspicious behaviour, and/or an admission-control policy that rejects non-compliant workloads when they are deployed (for example Falco or Tetragon for detection; Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper or Pod Security admission for admission control). Presence of committed policy, not a runtime guarantee.

dimensions.name: Malicious Dependencies
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any dependency the repository declares, in any ecosystem, is published as malicious rather than merely vulnerable: recorded by a vulnerability or malicious-package database as an attacker's work (for example an entry in the OpenSSF malicious-packages feed, or an advisory classified as embedded malicious code). Reported apart from Dependency Vulnerabilities (D30) because there is no safe version to upgrade to: the package must be removed and every credential it could have read rotated.

dimensions.name: Platform End-of-Life
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether anyone still ships security patches for the platform this repository RUNS ON — the runtime it pins and the framework majors its own constraints hold it to. Separate from D12 because the question differs: a current Django on an end-of-life Python is perfectly up to date and completely unsupported, and the fix is a migration rather than a version bump. What the repository says it merely SUPPORTS is never charged.

dimensions.name: Text alternatives
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether non-text content carries a text alternative — img/area/input[type=image] have alt, a meaningful svg has a title or aria-label, video has a captions track, and object/embed/canvas have a name or fallback content. Static markup readiness, not a WCAG conformance claim.

dimensions.name: Forms & labels
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether form fields (for example text inputs, selects and text areas) have a programmatic label (a label element associated with the field by reference or by wrapping it, aria-label or aria-labelledby), buttons have an accessible name (text content, aria-label or aria-labelledby), links have an accessible name, a non-interactive element (for example a div or span) that has a click handler and declares a control role gives that control an accessible name, fieldsets have a non-empty legend, a field component that takes its label through a property (for example a UI library's text-field component with a label prop) is given that property, and a placeholder is not used as the only label. A reading of the markup as written in source, not of the rendered page; not a WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) conformance claim.

dimensions.name: Page structure
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether pages declare a language (well-formed BCP-47) and a non-empty title, expose exactly one main landmark and a sane heading order with non-empty headings, keep zoom enabled, title their iframes, give data tables header cells, and avoid meta-refresh. Static markup readiness, not a WCAG conformance claim.

dimensions.name: Keyboard semantics
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether interactive behaviour can be reached and used from the keyboard: a non-interactive element (one with no native control behaviour, for example a div or span) that has a click handler has an accessibility role, a tab index and a keyboard handler; an element the repository's own style sheets give a pointer cursor has at least one of those three; an element whose only event handlers are a mouse enter/leave pair or a double-click can receive focus; no element has a positive tab index; no anchor lacks an href; and no link whose href is a placeholder (an empty fragment or a script URL, for example '#' or 'javascript:') acts as a button, that is, performs an action instead of navigating, through a click handler or through the script URL itself. A reading of the markup and styles as written in source, not of the running page; not a WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) conformance claim.

dimensions.name: ARIA correctness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether ARIA is used correctly — valid non-abstract roles, the ARIA state a role requires, valid (non-misspelled) aria-* attribute names, in-enum values for token-typed aria-* attributes, and no aria-hidden on (or wrapping) a focusable element. Static markup readiness, not a WCAG conformance claim.

dimensions.name: Visual & motion safety
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether focus outlines are not removed without a replacement focus style, motion (for example animations and transitions) is conditioned on the user's reduced-motion preference, and colour pairs written as literal values in the repository's own styles (including style tokens and utility classes that resolve to literal colours) meet a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1. Colours computed at runtime or loaded from outside the repository are not assessed. Static markup readiness, not a WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) conformance claim.

dimensions.name: Captive dependencies
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any singleton service captures a scoped/transient dependency — a silent lifetime/threading bug.

dimensions.name: Stateful singletons
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether singleton services avoid mutable shared instance state that concurrent callers would race on.

dimensions.name: Project dependency cycles
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the project-reference graph is acyclic (cycles block independent build/deploy and signal eroding boundaries).

dimensions.name: Dependency direction
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether dependencies point inward (Domain ← Application ← Infrastructure/Web) — the clean-architecture dependency rule, checked across the project graph.

dimensions.name: Architecture & structure
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the codebase has a recognisable, scale-appropriate structure (a named architectural style, or modular enough for its size) rather than being an ad-hoc ball of mud.

dimensions.name: Interface segregation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether interfaces stay focused rather than fat — the Interface-Segregation principle (SOLID 'I').

dimensions.name: Slice cohesion
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether feature slices stay independent (no direct cross-slice references) — the discipline that makes vertical-slice architecture pay off.

dimensions.name: Test isolation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether production projects stay free of references to test projects — tests may depend on production, never the reverse.

dimensions.name: CQS / query purity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether read (query) handlers stay side-effect-free — a query that writes persistent state or raises events breaks CQS and makes reads unsafe to retry, cache, or route to a read replica.

dimensions.name: Code composition
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How the code divides, by size, among five roles, each piece of code having one: domain (the code that models the business and holds its rules), application (the code that carries out use cases by directing the domain), infrastructure (the code that connects to the outside world, for example databases, networks, files and frameworks), test (the code that tests other code) and generated (code produced by a tool rather than written by hand). In domain-driven design terms, a small domain share beside a large infrastructure share suggests an anemic domain model, one whose types hold data while the business rules live elsewhere. A split by size, not proof of where the behaviour lives.

dimensions.name: Runtime unauthenticated reachability
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Of the screens reached by crawling with the application's own logged-in session, which ones also answer a GET carrying no credentials. Observed on the live app; GET only, and only URLs the crawl already fetched. Advisory; never scored.

dimensions.name: Runtime evidence locked — no reproducible boot
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the repository declares a way to boot the application: a compose file (with one service or several, for example a docker-compose file), an orchestration project that starts the application and its services (for example a .NET Aspire AppHost), or a container build file (for example a Dockerfile). The finding is raised when none is declared: then no evidence is gathered from the running application for the dimensions observed on it (rendered accessibility, outbound requests and security headers), though those dimensions may still have evidence from reading the code. A declared way to boot is not proof that the application builds or boots. Advisory: it explains missing runtime evidence and is never counted in any CAI score.

dimensions.name: Runtime readiness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How reproducibly this app can be booted for runtime evidence, plus the test frameworks detected. Advisory — never affects the score.

dimensions.name: Runtime security headers
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Which HTTP security headers the running application actually sets in its responses (for example Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy), observed while the application runs, never inferred from source. A header counts as set when a response carries it: the result records presence, not whether a value is strong (a policy that allows inline scripts still counts as set), and a deployment configured otherwise may send other headers. Advisory evidence for application security, for the secure-by-default requirements of the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) and for the cybersecurity risk-management measures of the NIS2 Directive; never counted in any CAI score.

dimensions.name: Runtime container hardening
dimensions.whatItMeasures: The confinement each container was actually started with — effective user, privileged mode, added and dropped capabilities, read-only root filesystem, no-new-privileges — read from the running stack rather than from a Dockerfile. Advisory; never scored.

dimensions.name: Runtime cookie security
dimensions.whatItMeasures: The HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite flags on the cookies the live application actually issued, read from its own responses. Advisory; never scored.

dimensions.name: Runtime API surface
dimensions.whatItMeasures: The API description the running application serves about itself, diffed against the one the repository commits, plus anonymous GET probes of its parameter-free operations. Templated paths and non-GET methods are listed as surface and never requested. Advisory; never scored.

dimensions.name: Runtime third-party data flows
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Third-party hosts the rendered UI tried to reach (analytics/trackers/CDNs), observed at render time — advisory evidence for GDPR data-protection-by-default. Never scored; jurisdiction/role never inferred.

dimensions.name: Runtime accessibility (rendered)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) success criteria checked on the page as a browser renders it, including those only a rendered page can show (for example contrast as displayed, focus order, and state that exists only once the page runs). A result counts only when it is reproducible: the same page rendered again gives the same result. Not a WCAG conformance claim: automated checks on a rendered page cover only part of the success criteria. Advisory: failures are reported as findings, never counted in any CAI score, and never change the static accessibility dimensions (AC1-AC6, which read the source without running it).

dimensions.name: Runtime exposed surface
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Every network binding the application actually opens when the stack the repository declares is started as declared, each with its service, container port, host port, protocol and bind scope (the addresses the port listens on, for example all interfaces or the local machine only), with any port the repository's own files never declare called out, for example one a base image opens. A port counts as declared when a file of the repository names it, for example a compose file's port mappings or a container build file's exposed ports. The bindings themselves are observed on the running application, never taken from those files, which serve only to tell declared ports from undeclared ones. An inventory, not a risk verdict: it does not say which networks can reach a port. Advisory: reported as evidence, never counted in any CAI score.

dimensions.name: Data Protection
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether sensitive data is encrypted at rest and in transit and keys are vaulted.

dimensions.name: Access Controls
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether access is authorized by default — a framework authorization attribute/decorator or policy, or imperative guard methods (throw-on-violation) called from handlers.

dimensions.name: Audit Trail
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether changes to sensitive data are recorded (who, what, when) for compliance + incident response.

dimensions.name: Data Retention
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether data has a defined lifetime — retention periods, TTLs, cleanup jobs (storage limitation).

dimensions.name: Data-Subject Rights
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether GDPR data-subject requests are supported in code — erasure, export/portability, consent.

dimensions.name: Aggregate boundaries
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether aggregates reference each other by identity (id) rather than by direct object reference — the core DDD consistency-boundary rule.

dimensions.name: Strongly-typed ids
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How much of the domain uses strongly-typed ids vs raw Guid/string/int — adoption curve, not all-or-nothing.

dimensions.name: Integration-event coupling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether cross-context integration events stay loosely coupled — no producer-owned enums/domain types leaking to consumers. Shared-kernel/contracts types are allowed.

dimensions.name: Rich vs anemic model
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether aggregates/entities carry the behaviour that protects their invariants, rather than being data bags driven by external services.

dimensions.name: Encapsulated state
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether entities (domain objects with an identity whose rules, or invariants, they must keep) protect their state, writable only inside the entity or when it is constructed, instead of exposing publicly writable state that bypasses those invariants, such as public setters or the entity's own mutable collections handed out directly rather than as a copy or read-only view. Softened where the code uses a persistence framework that rebuilds entities from stored state (for example Entity Framework or Marten).

dimensions.name: Domain ↔ infrastructure boundary
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the domain layer (the code that holds the business rules) stays free of infrastructure dependencies, for example persistence, database or cache clients, HTTP clients, web-framework or message-bus types: the clean-architecture dependency rule, that inner domain code never depends on outer infrastructure code.

dimensions.name: Repository granularity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether repositories are per aggregate root (not per child entity) so the root's invariants can't be bypassed.

dimensions.name: Value-object opportunities
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether clusters of primitives that travel together (a missing value object) are extracted. A low-weight suggestion.

dimensions.name: Scattered domain decisions
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether one domain rule is decided — or one measurement produced — in more than one place, rather than living on the type that owns it. A repeated judgement or a repeated derivation, not repeated text, so a clone detector cannot see either; and centralising the judgement does not fix the derivation, because two producers of the same numbers can disagree while every rule reading them is correct.

dimensions.name: One transaction, one aggregate
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a single operation mutates more than one aggregate root. An aggregate is a consistency boundary, so saving two together fuses them into one — the second's invariants come to depend on the first's transaction, and the pair can no longer be separated. Reads of other aggregates are not counted.

dimensions.name: Constructible invalid state
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether an aggregate can be constructed in a state its own rules forbid — a public constructor that takes a raw primitive, stores it, and validates nothing, with no factory beside it. A constructor taking only value objects is not counted: each parameter has already validated itself.

dimensions.name: Ambient inputs in the domain
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether domain types receive the time and randomness their rules depend on, rather than reading the process clock or a global random source directly — an ambient read makes the rule it feeds untestable at the instant that matters and lets two reads inside one operation disagree.

dimensions.name: Handler temporal coupling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether event handlers stay asynchronous (no blocking remote HTTP/gRPC calls awaited inside a handler).

dimensions.name: Event/command shape
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether commands have a single handler (one owner of the decision) and fan-out is modelled with events.

dimensions.name: Event naming
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether events are named in the past tense (a clarity nudge — low weight).

dimensions.name: Outbox / dual-write
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether state changes and message publishes are atomic (a transactional outbox) rather than a crash-unsafe dual write.

dimensions.name: Idempotency
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether retry-prone mutations (command handlers and message or event consumers) are idempotent, so an at-least-once redelivery or a client retry does not apply the effect twice.

dimensions.name: Fold determinism
dimensions.whatItMeasures: In event-sourced code, whether the functions that rebuild state from each stored event (event folds, for example in aggregates or projections, often named Apply or When) compute the new state only from the prior state and the event: without reading the current time, drawing a random number, generating a new identifier or doing I/O (input or output, for example reading a file, a database or the network). This is what makes replaying the same events always give the same state.

dimensions.name: Immutable events
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether persisted events are immutable facts (init-only/readonly) — a settable event member lets stored history be rewritten.

dimensions.name: PII in the event store
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the append-only event log avoids un-erasable personal data (or has a crypto-shredding strategy) — a GDPR right-to-erasure risk.

dimensions.name: Unfinished & placeholder code
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Leftovers of unfinished code (for example scaffolding, or AI coding-assistant output never completed) in production code, excluding tests and code emitted by a code generator (for example files marked as auto-generated): code that still throws an error marking it as not yet implemented (for example NotImplementedException in .NET), and placeholder string literals, that is, literals whose text stands in for real content still to be written (for example "TODO", "lorem ipsum", "changeme" or "your-api-key-here"). Scored on what the code shows, as a quality signal, never as a claim about who or what wrote it.

dimensions.name: Incompleteness & stubs
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Unfinished work recognised by the shape of the code, not by keywords such as TODO: members that only throw a not-implemented error, methods that take inputs and return a constant, asynchronous methods that never wait on anything, code disabled by a constant false condition in source or in conditional compilation (for example `if (false)` or `#if false`), and skeleton types most of whose members are unfinished in one of these ways.

dimensions.name: Personal-Data Handling (GDPR)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: The personal-data handling surface: fields that hold genuine personal data about a real person (not fiction, test or configuration data), surfaced for the GDPR Art. 25/32 self-assessment.

dimensions.name: Alt-Text Quality (WCAG 1.1.1)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether each image's alt text is a meaningful equivalent rather than a filename, a generic word or a placeholder. Complements the 'alt present?' check.

dimensions.name: Vulnerability-Disclosure Policy
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a SECURITY.md or security.txt is a real coordinated vulnerability-disclosure policy (a contact, how to report, how reports are handled), not a stub.

dimensions.name: Dev/Test/Prod Separation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether configuration separates development, test and production (distinct per-environment settings) rather than mixing them.

dimensions.name: Link & Button Text Quality (WCAG 2.4.4)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether each link's or button's text conveys its purpose out of context, rather than a vague 'click here' or 'read more'. Complements the 'has a name?' check.

dimensions.name: Heading & Label Text Quality (WCAG 2.4.6)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether each heading or label describes its section or field, rather than a placeholder ('Heading', 'Untitled', 'Label').

dimensions.name: Documentation (README)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the repository and its projects have a README, and whether it is substantive.

dimensions.name: Architecture documentation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether key decisions (ADRs) and the high-level shape (C4/diagrams) are written down.

dimensions.name: Folder & project structure
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the repository is organised deliberately: production code and tests are set apart in a way its ecosystem or the repository itself declares.

dimensions.name: Documentation accuracy
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the project's current-state documentation describes the code that exists.

dimensions.name: CI/CD gates
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether an automated pipeline builds and tests every change.

dimensions.name: Observability
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code is diagnosable in production — structured logging, tracing/metrics, health checks.

dimensions.name: Security & performance tooling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether SAST, secret/dependency scanning and performance benchmarking are wired in (presence, not runtime).

dimensions.name: Deployment & Rollback
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether releases are automated and safely reversible (probes, rolling updates, approval gates) — from manifests/pipeline files, not the live environment.

dimensions.name: DR & Backup
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether disaster recovery is planned and codified — backups, geo-recovery, RTO/RPO, persistence guarantees — from IaC + container manifests + docs, never the live cloud.

dimensions.name: Release Hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether releases are traceable — a maintained changelog and explicit version stamping.

dimensions.name: Outbound HTTP resilience
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether outbound HTTP calls are wrapped in resilience (retry/timeout/circuit-breaker) so a failing dependency doesn't cascade.

dimensions.name: Schema migrations
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether database schema changes in production code and configuration go through versioned migrations (a committed, ordered history of schema changes) rather than being created or altered automatically from the application's entity or model definitions (for example EF Core EnsureCreated, GORM AutoMigrate, SQLAlchemy create_all, TypeORM synchronize set to true, Hibernate ddl-auto set to create or update). Test code, for example a fixture that creates a throwaway database, is excluded. A positive result means production schema changes are recorded as versioned migrations and not created automatically; it is not proof that the migrations are applied or match the live schema.

dimensions.name: Domain vs controller coverage
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether test coverage falls on the domain layer (the business rules) rather than on the web or controller layer, the code that receives requests and hands them to the domain and should hold little logic of its own.

dimensions.name: Library API & versioning
dimensions.whatItMeasures: For a library: a deliberate (small) public API surface and explicit semantic versioning so consumers can depend on it safely.

dimensions.name: BDD / executable specs
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether behaviour is captured as executable Gherkin specifications (a plus for shared understanding) — only assessed when a BDD framework is present.

dimensions.name: CI test-gate honesty
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the CI gate executes the test inventory it appears to have: excluded suites, skipped tests, and coverage collected without a threshold.

dimensions.name: Benchmark discipline
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code protects its performance with benchmarks — a benchmark suite, allocation/memory measurement, and (ideally) a CI gate. Presence is credited as a bonus, never a deduction.

dimensions.name: Allocation hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code is written to minimise allocations so it doesn't pressure its host's memory manager — buffer/slice views over copies, object pooling, stack or value-type allocation, and buffer writers. Reward-only: credited where present, never penalised where a simpler style is fine.

dimensions.name: Async & latency hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether asynchronous work in production code (tests excluded) is kept from blocking a thread or event loop. Two things count. First, a synchronous wait for asynchronous work to finish (sync-over-async): in .NET anywhere in production code, not only inside async methods (for example .Wait() or .GetAwaiter().GetResult() on a task), because a blocked thread can deadlock the very work it waits for; in other languages where the wait sits inside asynchronous code (for example block_on in a Rust async function, runBlocking in a Kotlin suspend function, or block() inside a reactive publisher). Second, a blocking call made inside asynchronous code (for example a blocking sleep or HTTP call inside a Python coroutine, or a synchronous file call inside an async JavaScript function). Either stalls a thread or loop and risks deadlock. And where the code is a reusable .NET library (code packaged for other applications to use), its awaits do not resume on the caller's captured context (for example by using ConfigureAwait(false)), so the library does not deadlock or stall a caller that blocks on it.

dimensions.name: Type Safety
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How much of the frontend is typed TypeScript vs untyped JavaScript.

dimensions.name: Cyclomatic Complexity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Per-function complexity of the frontend code, counted from each function's actual branching: cyclomatic complexity, one plus each decision point (a condition, a loop, a case label or a short-circuit boolean operator); and cognitive complexity, one increment for each if, else-if, else, conditional expression, switch, loop, catch, labelled jump, recursive call and run of the same boolean operator, plus, for the structures that nest (conditionals, conditional expressions, switches, loops and catches), one more for each level of nesting they sit in.

dimensions.name: Large Files
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How many source files exceed the large-file threshold.

dimensions.name: Test Coverage
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Static test reachability: the share of production files that at least one test reaches by following imports, directly or through other imported files, found without running anything. It is not runtime line or branch coverage.

dimensions.name: Dependency Freshness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How outdated the npm dependencies are (a maturity signal). JS/npm CVEs are scored separately in D30 (JS/npm Dependency Vulnerabilities).

dimensions.name: Tooling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the project wires up each of test, lint and type-check runs: in a package.json script, judged by the command the script runs (for example eslint, tsc, vitest, jest or playwright) rather than by its name, so a script named test that runs no test tool does not count; or in a CI (continuous integration) workflow that invokes such a tool, so a tool run only in CI also counts. The presence of that wiring, not evidence that the checks run or pass.

dimensions.name: Dead Code
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Dead code: files that cannot be reached by following imports, directly or through other files, from any entry point (an application start file, a tooling or configuration file, or a test), and exports that no file in the repository imports. Tests count as entry points, not as candidates. A file loaded only by a framework convention rather than an import (for example a route file found by its folder) can appear here, so a finding is not proof that the file is unused.

dimensions.name: Dependency Hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether an npm package's declared dependencies match what its code uses: dependencies its package.json declares that the code does not use, packages the code imports (by any form of loading, for example import or require) that are not declared anywhere, and packages needed only for types or tests (for example @types packages or a test runner) declared as production dependencies rather than development dependencies. Built-in runtime modules and relative imports of the package's own files are not packages. Not a check of whether dependencies are outdated, vulnerable or licensed.

dimensions.name: Circular Imports
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Import cycles in the module graph of the frontend code (the code of the user interface that runs in the browser or another client): source files that import each other in a loop, directly (two files importing each other) or through others (A imports B, B imports C, C imports A), so they can only be understood and changed together.

dimensions.name: Code Duplication
dimensions.whatItMeasures: The share of the frontend code's production lines inside a near-exact copy-pasted block of substantial extent, each line counted once. A copied block counts where its copies still agree on most of their own identifiers and literal values, or were renamed as they were pasted but kept most of their constants; and where, in addition, the copies either carry enough code to stand on their own (more than a small declaration such as a list of fields or imports) or the copied extent reaches 30 lines. The exact shares and minimum size are stated on the dimension page. A re-implementation sharing neither names nor values, and a small pasted declaration, are not counted, so a clean R10 (no such block found) is not a claim that nothing was copied.

dimensions.name: Import Boundaries
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether imports in the frontend code respect the boundaries of the architecture layout the code follows, either a feature-sliced layout (code split into ordered layers, each split into slices by feature or business area, where code in a slice may import from its own slice and from lower layers, never from another slice of its own layer, and reaches another slice only through that slice's public entry point) or a layered src directory (where a layer imports only from the layers it is built on); and whether one package imports another package's internal files instead of its public entry point (a deep import).

dimensions.name: Web-Security Posture
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Transport security, security headers, secure cookies, input validation, middleware order and crypto hygiene (presence, not runtime).

dimensions.name: Supply-chain hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the repository pins its dependencies: for each ecosystem it uses (one with a package manifest in the repository), whether the dependency versions are fixed in a committed file, either a lockfile or one shared file fixing the versions for every project of that ecosystem (for example .NET's central package management), so that a build resolves the same versions every time. Evidence toward practice PW.4 of the NIST SSDF (Secure Software Development Framework) and toward SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts). Pinning committed in the repository does not prove that the build uses it, that the build is reproducible bit for bit, or that it reaches any SLSA level. Advisory: reported, never scored.

dimensions.name: Async correctness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code avoids sync-over-async (deadlock-prone blocking on tasks) and async void.

dimensions.name: Cancellation propagation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether asynchronous methods in production code accept a cancellation token or signal (for example a CancellationToken in .NET or an AbortSignal in JavaScript), so their work can be cancelled (adoption curve). Methods whose signature a framework fixes (for example overrides or UI event handlers) are not counted unless they take one. Accepting one does not show that it is passed on to the work the method starts or honoured there.

dimensions.name: Exception handling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether exceptions are handled rather than silently swallowed or rethrown with lost stack traces.

dimensions.name: Structured logging
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether log calls use message templates (queryable) rather than interpolated strings.

dimensions.name: Nullable reference types
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether C# nullable reference types (the compiler's checks that a reference may be null) are enabled for the code (for example by a project setting or a `#nullable enable` directive), and not undermined by heavy use of the null-forgiving operator (`!`), which silences those checks.

dimensions.name: Hand-rolled structured-format parsing
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether JSON or XML text is parsed by hand with regular expressions or string operations (for example pulling a value out by matching its key or tag), while a dedicated parser for that same format (for example a parsing library, or the language's standard-library module) is already referenced in the same project or build unit (for example a package or module), as a dependency or by an import in its code: a common source of silent data bugs.

dimensions.name: Silent fallback defaults
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether parse/lookup failure paths return hard-coded constants with no logging or throw — failures that convert data errors into silent behavior changes.

dimensions.name: JS interop contract
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether string-named JS interop bindings resolve against the first-party JavaScript, and whether anything guards the boundary against renames.

dimensions.name: Subsumed condition operand
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether, in a chain of conditions joined by logical or (`||`) or logical and (`&&`), one operand logically implies another, so one of them can never change the chain's value (under or, the operand that implies the other adds nothing; under and, the implied one restricts nothing): the condition tests less than it reads, which usually means a different condition was intended.

dimensions.name: Duplicated predicate
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether one non-trivial boolean expression (at least 40 characters long, whitespace aside) is written out the same, character for character apart from whitespace, in two or more files: a copy too short for Code Duplication (D4) to count.

dimensions.name: Unreachable branch
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any branch is dead by construction, that is, can never run whatever the input, from the code alone: a switch label that can never equal the switch's subject because the code converts the subject to one letter case and the label has letters in the other case (for example an upper-case or mixed-case label against a lower-cased subject); or an else-if arm whose condition can be true only when the condition of an earlier arm in the same chain is also true, so every input that would satisfy it is already taken by that earlier arm (for example an earlier test that a string contains "ab" before a later test that it contains "abc"). An arm that only partly overlaps an earlier one is not dead. Not a general dead-code or coverage measure.

dimensions.name: Undrained process stream
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a child process with BOTH standard streams redirected drains both — reading one to the end while the other is never read deadlocks once the child fills the unread pipe.

dimensions.name: Bypassable address classification
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a hand-rolled public/private IP check can be walked past — a method that unwraps IPv4-mapped IPv6 but returns the opposite verdict for the same host written as IPv4-compatible, 6to4 or NAT64.

dimensions.name: Unvalidated length from an untrusted reader
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a length read out of the stream being parsed is bounded before it is allocated or read — an unchecked count taken from the input lets the input choose the allocation.

dimensions.name: Unfloored truncation loop
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a loop that shortens a string until it fits a length budget (the greatest length the string may have) has a floor: anything that ends the shortening no later than when the string is empty, in the loop condition or as a guard or exit (a break, return or throw) in its body. A direct comparison of the string's own length with the budget (for example length greater than the budget) is a floor, and so is a test that the string is not empty. A comparison in which the string's length is only one term is not a floor when the other terms alone can exceed the budget (for example its length plus a suffix's length compared with the budget, where the suffix alone can be longer than the budget). A loop with no floor grinds the value down to the empty string and then past it: into a substring request with a negative length, which fails at run time in some languages, or, where the language clamps it, a loop that never ends.

dimensions.name: Uncapped recursion over a caller-supplied document
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a walk that recurses through a JSON or XML tree handed in by its caller bounds how deep it will go (for example with a depth or remaining-levels value carried through each recursive call): an uncapped walk lets the document's nesting choose the stack depth, and the resulting stack overflow in some runtimes (for example .NET) cannot be caught and ends the process.

dimensions.name: Disposal-pattern correctness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a type's disposal matches what it OWNS — releasing what it created, leaving alone what it was handed, and not declaring a finalizer for state that has nothing unmanaged to finalize.

dimensions.name: Unrestored process-global state
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a method that temporarily changes state belonging to the whole process — the working directory, an environment variable — puts it back on EVERY path: a restore reached only when nothing throws leaks the change to the rest of the process.

dimensions.name: Mistyped argument guard
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether an argument guard throws the exception its own condition describes: a guard that rejects a value for being empty and reports it as a null argument (for example ArgumentNullException in .NET, or a type derived from it) tells the caller a parameter was null when it provably was not.

dimensions.name: Side-effecting pattern guard
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a pattern-match guard (in C#, the `when` clause of a switch case or switch-expression arm) is free of side effects: a guard that increments, decrements or assigns while deciding whether its arm matches applies that change during pattern matching, on an arm that may not be selected, and skips it entirely when it sits where a short-circuiting operator in the guard can skip it (the right operand of and, or or null-coalescing, a branch of a conditional, or after a null-conditional access) and that operator answers first.

dimensions.name: Contradicted release guard
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a method that itself takes a lock or semaphore, and gives it back in an always-run cleanup block (for example `finally`) only as a true/false flag directs, returns a success or failure result that agrees with the flag's state at that return: success means the caller still holds the lock or semaphore, failure means the cleanup gives it back. A mismatch either lets a second caller past the exclusion or leaves the lock or semaphore held with nothing to ever give it back.

dimensions.name: Unguarded diagnostic materialisation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether, in production code (tests excluded), the work a diagnostic log line costs is paid only when that line is wanted: where a call's arguments are evaluated before the call, a trace, debug or verbose message whose arguments do work that scales with a collection (for example joining, projecting or serialising it) is built in full every time the call runs, and then discarded by a level the shipped configuration leaves switched off, unless the work is deferred into a function the logger calls only when the level is on, or a check of the log level, a build switch or conditional compilation keeps it from running.

dimensions.name: Document value interpolated into markup unescaped
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether text read out of the document being converted is escaped before it is written into generated markup — a value the document's author chose, interpolated into an attribute the surrounding literal delimits, can close that attribute and open another.

dimensions.name: Inert configuration knob
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a value the caller is invited to supply is the value the type actually uses: a constructor parameter stored in a private field that nothing reads, while the default it was given is written out again where the field should have been read; a lookup by key that falls back to a different setting than the one its key names, while elsewhere the same type falls back to the matching setting for that same key; or a culture-sensitive parse given no culture by a type that passes its own settable culture to the same kind of parse elsewhere. In each case a value someone supplies is silently replaced by another.

dimensions.name: Unsynchronised callback handoff
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a value handed from a callback (for example an event handler) to the code waiting on it is passed through a structure made for concurrent use, under a lock, or otherwise without the callback and the outside code touching the same collection at overlapping times. A collection not made for concurrent use (for example a plain queue, list or dictionary) that the callback changes and that is also accessed outside the callback while the callback can still run is used by both at the same time. A semaphore, completion object or other wait handle beside it orders what the callback wrote before raising it, but does not protect an outside access that a run of the callback can overlap, including one made before the code waits for the run in progress; an outside access that no run of the callback can overlap (for example after the waiting code has observed the callback's final signal, when the callback no longer touches the collection after signalling) is not this.

dimensions.name: Collection changed while being enumerated
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a C# `foreach` leaves the collection it is walking alone: a body that adds to or removes from the very collection the loop is enumerating invalidates the enumerator the loop holds, so the next `MoveNext` throws `InvalidOperationException` and the remaining items are never seen. Collections whose enumerator survives such a change (for example concurrent or immutable collections, and arrays), and a change the loop exits straight after, are not this.

dimensions.name: Index access outside its own emptiness guard
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a condition that tests a value for emptiness (for example a null-or-empty check, a length or count compared with a constant, or an any-element check) indexes that same value only where the test has established that it is not empty: for example, an or placed one parenthesis too far to the left can leave one index access outside the guard while another stays inside it, so the empty case the guard exists to anticipate reaches the index and fails.

dimensions.name: Per-element action decided by a fixed element
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a decision taken once per element is taken ABOUT that element — a test inside a counted loop that reads a fixed subscript of the very collection its guarded statement indexes by the loop variable applies element zero's answer to all of them, so the elements that differ from it are all handled wrongly, and in the same direction.

dimensions.name: Support guard that admits what it rejects
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a guard written as the negation of a logical OR of two or more terms, which mixes capabilities the code needs (for example true/false flags) with a fault it refuses (for example a test that a value is not equal to a constant), says what its author meant. By De Morgan's law the negation of an OR is the AND of the negated terms, so, for example, `!(a || b || x != k)` with `k` a constant means `!a && !b && x == k`: an early-exit guard (one that leaves before the code it protects) turns inside out, firing only where every capability is absent and the value equals the constant, and letting every value the fault term was meant to refuse (here every x other than k) into the code that cannot handle it, whatever the capabilities. A negated OR whose terms are all capabilities or all faults is not this; a finding marks logic that contradicts the guard's evident intent, not a confirmed runtime failure.

dimensions.name: Test-only surface in a production module
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether an Erlang production module publishes functions that exist only for its tests: Erlang has no visibility below `-export`, so a test helper exported unconditionally becomes part of the module's contract for every caller in the system, instead of being exported inside an `-ifdef(TEST)` section that keeps it out of the shipped module.

dimensions.name: Type resolved by simple name across every loaded assembly
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a plugin lookup names the type it means: searching the types of every assembly loaded into the process for one whose simple name (without its namespace) equals a string supplied at run time, and taking the first one found, is decided by the order the assemblies were loaded rather than by the source, so the same name can resolve to a different type on the next run. A lookup that requires exactly one match, or that requires the full name (with its namespace) to match as well as the simple name, is not this; one that accepts either name still is.
